STEP 1 - Scene: This is a simple plate of whole foods. It holds plain white rice, two corn-on-the-cob rounds, raw cauliflower florets and a whole apple.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A red dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: I can see five foods and no visible oil or sauce.
- Cooked white rice
- Corn on the cob (2 rounds)
- Cauliflower florets
- Apple (whole)

STEP 4 - Area: Food covers about 54% of the plate.
- Rice: ~12%
- Corn: ~8% (two rounds about 7 cm across, each ~38 cm²)
- Cauliflower: ~22%
- Apple: ~12% (about 8 cm across, ~50 cm², measured larger than the 7 cm I first assumed)

STEP 5 - Volume (area × height):
- Rice: 64 cm² × 1.5 cm = 96 ml
- Corn: 77 cm² × 3 cm = 231 ml, but with the cob share this is too high, so I use the rounds directly. Each is about 3 cm tall, giving roughly 60 ml each.
- Cauliflower: 117 cm² × 3 cm = 350 ml
- Apple: treated as a whole fruit of about 8 cm diameter

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Rice: 96 ml × 0.8 = 77 g
- Corn: about 50 g each with cob, roughly 30 g edible each, so ~60 g edible total
- Cauliflower: 350 ml × 0.5 = 175 g. Florets are airy, so I keep the low end, about 150 g.
- Apple: about 180 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Rice: 77 g × 130 kcal/100 g = 100 kcal
- Corn: 60 g × 96 kcal/100 g = 58 kcal
- Cauliflower: 150 g × 25 kcal/100 g = 38 kcal
- Apple: 180 g × 52 kcal/100 g = 94 kcal

Total ≈ 467 g, about 290 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The plate is only about half covered with light foods, so a low total is plausible.
